library(nlmixr2lib)

library(dplyr)

# Model and source

```{r model-meta, include = FALSE}
mod_pre <- readModelDb("Masroor_2019_ISIS325568_pretreatment")
mod_post <- readModelDb("Masroor_2019_ISIS325568_posttreatment")
ui_pre <- rxode2::rxode(mod_pre)
ui_post <- rxode2::rxode(mod_post)
```

* Citation: `r ui_pre$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1007/s10928-019-09655-2> (open access, PMC6868112)
* Supplement: Electronic Supplementary Material 1 (PDF), published with the
  article. It holds the smooth-profiling estimation details, the
  identifiability analysis and Table 7, the per-subject parameter estimates.
* Clinical study: van Dongen MG et al. (2015) First proof of pharmacology in
  humans of a novel glucagon receptor antisense drug. J Clin Pharmacol
  55(3):298-306, <https://doi.org/10.1002/jcph.396>.

Masroor 2019 builds a small mechanistic model of the glucagon challenge test:
three plasma compartments (glucose `G`, insulin `I`, glucagon `E`) coupled to a
hepatic glucagon-receptor sub-model in which the receptor binds glucagon,
internalizes, and recycles. Hepatic glucose production (HGP) is a Hill function
of the glucagon-bound receptor fraction. The model is used to interpret
challenge tests performed in eight healthy volunteers before and after six
weeks of ISIS 325568 400 mg/week, a 2'-O-methoxyethyl antisense oligonucleotide
that lowers hepatic glucagon-receptor (GCGR) expression.

The authors fitted each subject's pre- and post-treatment challenge
**separately** with the smooth profiling method of Ramsay et al. (no
mixed-effects model), and report the mean and SD of the individual estimates
for each condition (Table 4). The library therefore carries two models with
the same structure:

| Model | Parameter set |
|---|---|
| `Masroor_2019_ISIS325568_pretreatment` | Table 4 "Before" averages |
| `Masroor_2019_ISIS325568_posttreatment` | Table 4 "After" averages |

Both are deterministic typical-value models: the reported SDs are the spread
of individual fits, not population variances, and the fitting method has no
residual-error model.

# Population

Eight healthy volunteers (subjects 30, 31, 32, 33, 35, 36, 38 and 40) of the
400 mg/week multiple-dose cohort of van Dongen 2015, each studied with a 6-h
glucagon challenge before treatment and after six weeks (eight doses) of ISIS
325568. Masroor 2019 does not report demographics. Glucose, insulin and
glucagon were measured every 15 min during the challenge (135 to 360 min).

```{r population}
str(mod_pre()$population)
```

# The glucagon challenge test and the model time axis

The test lasts 6 h. During hours 0-3 the subject is at steady state. At hour 3
somatostatin stops endogenous insulin and glucagon secretion and three
constant infusions start (Table 3): glucose 0.24 g/h, insulin 480 mU/h and
glucagon 4134.7 pmol/h, which raises plasma glucagon 2-3-fold.

The packaged models describe the challenge period, Eq 8a-8e of the paper.
**Model time 0 is test hour 3**; every state starts at the pre-challenge steady
state (Eq 7 and Eq 9), and endogenous secretion is zero throughout. Supply the
three infusions as dosing events starting at time 0 into the `glucose`,
`insulin` and `glucagon` states (amounts in g, mU and pmol). The plasma states
are carried as amounts (concentration times distribution volume) so that an
infusion of `Q` per hour contributes `Q / V` to the concentration, exactly the
paper's `QG/VG`, `QI/VI` and `QE/VE` terms.

The pre-challenge steady state is computed inside the model from the
parameters. The baseline glucagon and insulin concentrations are model
parameters (`bl_glucagon`, `bl_insulin`); the receptor fractions follow from
Eq 6, and baseline glucose is the positive root of Eq 9 (HGP equals total
glucose consumption). The source does not tabulate the average baselines, so
`bl_glucagon` and `bl_insulin` were digitised by the maintainers from the 0-3 h
segment of the average-parameter curves in Figure 5.

# Source trace

Per-parameter provenance is recorded as an in-file comment next to each
`ini()` entry in `inst/modeldb/specificDrugs/Masroor_2019_ISIS325568_*.R`.

| Parameter (file) | Paper symbol | Before | After | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `lhgp_base` | bG (g/L/h) | 0.0804 | 0.18 | Table 4 |
| `lvmax_hgp` | V1 | 5.63 | 6.81 | Table 4 |
| `lre50_hgp` | K1' = K1/Rtot | 0.00501 | 0.0109 | Table 4 |
| `hill` | n | 2 (fixed) | 2 (fixed) | Methods, "The hepatic glucose production rate" |
| `lvmax_ii` | Vii | 0.896 | 0.936 | Table 4 |
| `km_ii` | Kii (g/L) | 0 (fixed) | 0 (fixed) | Table 2; Methods (collapsed to zero) |
| `lvmax_id` | Vid | 1.52 | 1.66 | Table 4 |
| `lkm_id` | Kid (g/L) | 11 | 10.3 | Table 4 |
| `lkdeg_insulin` | kdegI (1/h) | 30.5 | 30.9 | Table 4 |
| `lkdeg_glucagon` | kdegE (1/h) | 5.73 | 5.76 | Table 4 |
| `lkint` | kin (1/h) | 21.5 | 12.1 | Table 4 |
| `lvh` | Vh (L) | 4.65 | 4.96 | Table 4 |
| `lkon` | kon (1/pmol/h) | 0.0036 (fixed) | 0.0036 (fixed) | Table 2; Methods; supplement Table 7 footnote |
| `lkoff` | koff (1/h) | 14.4 (fixed) | 14.4 (fixed) | Table 2; Methods (0.24 1/min) |
| `lkrec` | krec (1/h) | 0.18 (fixed) | 0.18 (fixed) | Table 2; Methods (0.003 1/min) |
| `kint_free` | kin' (1/h) | 0 (fixed) | 0 (fixed) | Table 2; Methods (collapsed to zero) |
| `lv_glucose` | VG (L) | 4.44 (fixed) | 4.44 (fixed) | Table 3 |
| `lv_insulin` | VI (L) | 1.52 (fixed) | 1.52 (fixed) | Table 3 |
| `lv_glucagon` | VE (L) | 19.6 (fixed) | 19.6 (fixed) | Table 3 (Table 2 prints 9.6; see below) |
| `bl_glucagon` | E-bar (pmol/L) | 17.4 | 24.0 | digitised, Figure 5 E panels, 0-3 h |
| `bl_insulin` | I-bar (mU/L) | 10.5 | 9.7 | digitised, Figure 5 I panels, 0-3 h |

| Equation | Source |
|---|---|
| `d/dt(glucose)`: infusion + HGP - Vii G/(Kii+G) - Vid I G/(Kid+G) | Eq 3 / Eq 8a |
| `d/dt(insulin)`: infusion - kdegI I (secretion off) | Eq 1 / Eq 8b |
| `d/dt(glucagon)`: infusion - kdegE E (secretion off) | Eq 2 / Eq 8c |
| `d/dt(target_gcgr_liver)` (free receptor fraction r) | Eq 5 / Eq 8d |
| `d/dt(complex_gcgr_liver)` (bound receptor fraction re) | Eq 5 / Eq 8e |
| `fhgp = bG + V1 re^2 / (K1'^2 + re^2)` | Methods, "The hepatic glucose production rate" |
| Initial receptor fractions r-bar, re-bar | Eq 6 / Eq 7d-7e |
| Initial glucose G-bar | Eq 9 (HGP = consumption at steady state) |

## Units

| Term | Units |
|---|---|
| `Gc`, `Ic`, `GNc` | g/L, mU/L, pmol/L |
| `fhgp`, `hgp_base`, `vmax_hgp`, `vmax_ii` | g/L/h |
| `vmax_id * Ic * Gc / (km_id + Gc)` | g/L/h, so `vmax_id` is 1/h per mU/L |
| `kon * vh * GNc` | (1/pmol/h) x L x pmol/L = 1/h |
| `koff`, `kint`, `krec`, `kint_free`, `kdeg_*` | 1/h |
| `d/dt(glucose)` = `v_glucose` x (g/L/h) | g/h |
| `d/dt(target_gcgr_liver)`, `d/dt(complex_gcgr_liver)` | fraction/h |

Tables 1 and 4 print the units of V1 and Vii as 1/h. With the receptor
fraction dimensionless and the glucose equation in g/L/h, both must be g/L/h
(Vii is the whole insulin-independent rate once Kii = 0); the values are
unaffected.

# Simulating the challenge

```{r simulate}
challenge_events <- function() {
  rxode2::et(amt = 0.24 * 3, rate = 0.24, cmt = "glucose") |>
    rxode2::et(amt = 480 * 3, rate = 480, cmt = "insulin") |>
    rxode2::et(amt = 4134.7 * 3, rate = 4134.7, cmt = "glucagon") |>
    rxode2::et(seq(0, 3, by = 0.05), cmt = "glucose")
}

out_cols <- c("time", "Gc", "Ic", "GNc", "r_free", "r_bound", "r_internal", "fhgp")
sim_pre <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_pre, challenge_events())
sim_post <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_post, challenge_events())

sim <- bind_rows(
  as.data.frame(sim_pre)[, out_cols] |> mutate(treatment = "Before treatment"),
  as.data.frame(sim_post)[, out_cols] |> mutate(treatment = "After treatment (400 mg)")
) |>
  mutate(test_time = time + 3)

# The 0-3 h baseline period is the steady state the models start from.
baseline <- sim |>
  filter(time == 0) |>
  select(-time, -test_time) |>
  tidyr::crossing(test_time = seq(0, 3, by = 0.25))
sim_6h <- bind_rows(baseline, sim |> select(-time)) |>
  mutate(treatment = factor(treatment, c("Before treatment", "After treatment (400 mg)")))
```

## Figure 5

```{r figure-5, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 5 of Masroor 2019: model solution with the average before- and after-treatment parameters (Table 4). The dashed line marks the start of the challenge."}
sim_6h |>
  mutate(re_x10 = 10 * r_bound) |>
  select(treatment, test_time, Gc, Ic, GNc, r_free, re_x10, r_internal, fhgp) |>
  pivot_longer(-c(treatment, test_time)) |>
  mutate(
    panel = case_when(
      name == "Gc" ~ "G (g/L)",
      name == "Ic" ~ "I (mU/L)",
      name == "GNc" ~ "E (pmol/L)",
      name %in% c("r_free", "re_x10", "r_internal") ~ "R / Rtot",
      name == "fhgp" ~ "Fhgp (g/L/h)"
    ),
    panel = factor(panel, c("G (g/L)", "I (mU/L)", "E (pmol/L)", "R / Rtot", "Fhgp (g/L/h)")),
    series = recode(name, r_free = "r", re_x10 = "10 re", r_internal = "ri", .default = "model")
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(test_time, value, colour = series)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 3, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  facet_grid(panel ~ treatment, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = 0:6) +
  labs(x = "Time in the challenge test (h)", y = NULL, colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw()
```

The model curves are compared below with values digitised by the maintainers
from the average-parameter curves of Figure 5 (green lines; the receptor panel
gives the free fraction `r`). Model and figure come from the same equations
and the same parameters, so the remaining differences are digitisation error
(one pixel is about 0.04 g/L, 1 pmol/L, 0.01 receptor fraction and 0.06 g/L/h).

```{r figure-5-digitised}
fig5 <- tribble(
  ~treatment, ~test_time, ~Gc, ~GNc, ~r_free, ~fhgp,
  "Before treatment", 3.5, 1.660, 35.8, 0.479, 4.15,
  "Before treatment", 4.0, 2.128, 36.8, 0.447, 4.02,
  "Before treatment", 4.5, 2.340, 37.4, 0.415, 3.86,
  "Before treatment", 5.0, 2.426, 36.8, 0.394, 3.73,
  "Before treatment", 5.5, 2.426, 37.4, 0.378, 3.61,
  "After treatment (400 mg)", 3.5, 1.362, 36.3, 0.457, 3.64,
  "After treatment (400 mg)", 4.0, 1.617, 36.8, 0.436, 3.61,
  "After treatment (400 mg)", 4.5, 1.745, 36.8, 0.426, 3.48,
  "After treatment (400 mg)", 5.0, 1.766, 36.8, 0.415, 3.39,
  "After treatment (400 mg)", 5.5, 1.766, 36.8, 0.404, 3.29
) |>
  pivot_longer(c(Gc, GNc, r_free, fhgp), names_to = "output", values_to = "figure_5")

cmp_fig5 <- sim_6h |>
  mutate(test_time = round(test_time, 2), treatment = as.character(treatment)) |>
  select(treatment, test_time, Gc, GNc, r_free, fhgp) |>
  pivot_longer(c(Gc, GNc, r_free, fhgp), names_to = "output", values_to = "model") |>
  inner_join(fig5, by = c("treatment", "test_time", "output")) |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (model - figure_5) / figure_5)

cmp_fig5 |>
  mutate(across(c(model, figure_5), \(x) signif(x, 3)), pct_diff = round(pct_diff, 1)) |>
  rename(
    Treatment = treatment, "Test time (h)" = test_time, Output = output,
    Model = model, "Figure 5" = figure_5, "Difference (%)" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable()

stopifnot(
  abs(median(cmp_fig5$pct_diff)) < 3,
  max(abs(cmp_fig5$pct_diff)) < 6
)
```

# Steady-state and mass-balance checks

At model time 0 both models must sit at the steady state of Eq 7: HGP equals
total glucose consumption (Eq 9), and the receptor equations balance at the
baseline glucagon concentration.

```{r steady-state}
ss_check <- function(sim, ui) {
  p <- ui$theta
  s0 <- as.data.frame(sim)[1, ]
  e0 <- s0$GNc
  kon <- exp(p[["lkon"]])
  koff <- exp(p[["lkoff"]])
  krec <- exp(p[["lkrec"]])
  kint <- exp(p[["lkint"]])
  vh <- exp(p[["lvh"]])
  consumption <- exp(p[["lvmax_ii"]]) * s0$Gc / (p[["km_ii"]] + s0$Gc) +
    exp(p[["lvmax_id"]]) * s0$Ic * s0$Gc / (exp(p[["lkm_id"]]) + s0$Gc)
  dr <- -kon * vh * e0 * s0$r_free + koff * s0$r_bound - p[["kint_free"]] * s0$r_free +
    krec * (1 - s0$r_free - s0$r_bound)
  dre <- kon * vh * e0 * s0$r_free - (koff + kint) * s0$r_bound
  data.frame(
    G0 = s0$Gc, HGP = s0$fhgp, consumption = consumption,
    dr_dt = dr, dre_dt = dre
  )
}
ss <- bind_rows(
  "Before treatment" = ss_check(sim_pre, ui_pre),
  "After treatment (400 mg)" = ss_check(sim_post, ui_post),
  .id = "treatment"
)
knitr::kable(ss, digits = 6)
stopifnot(
  all(abs(ss$HGP - ss$consumption) < 1e-8),
  all(abs(ss$dr_dt) < 1e-10),
  all(abs(ss$dre_dt) < 1e-10)
)
```

The baseline glucose that Eq 9 implies (`G0`) is not an input. It agrees
with the 0-3 h level of Figure 5 (about 1.06 g/L before and 1.00 g/L after
treatment, digitised) to within a few percent, which confirms the
steady-state relations and the digitised baselines together. The check allows
8%: `G0` moves about 1.1% for every 1% change in the digitised insulin
baseline, and one pixel of the Figure 5 insulin axis is about 3% of
`bl_insulin`, so two pixels of reading error in insulin alone account for the
6% gap after treatment.

```{r baseline-glucose}
g0_cmp <- data.frame(
  treatment = ss$treatment,
  model_G0 = ss$G0,
  figure_5 = c(1.06, 1.00)
) |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (model_G0 - figure_5) / figure_5)
knitr::kable(g0_cmp, digits = 3)
stopifnot(all(abs(g0_cmp$pct_diff) < 8))
```

During the challenge, insulin settles at `QI / (VI kdegI)` and glucagon at
`QE / (VE kdegE)`; with VE = 19.6 L the glucagon plateau is about 37 pmol/L,
the level Figure 5 shows.

```{r plateaus}
plateau <- sim |>
  group_by(treatment) |>
  filter(time == max(time)) |>
  select(treatment, Ic, GNc)
knitr::kable(plateau, digits = 2)
stopifnot(
  abs(plateau$GNc[plateau$treatment == "Before treatment"] - 4134.7 / (19.6 * 5.73)) < 0.05,
  abs(plateau$Ic[plateau$treatment == "Before treatment"] - 480 / (1.52 * 30.5)) < 0.01
)
```

# Reproducing the paper's analysis

**Loss of glucagon receptors.** Since K1' = K1/Rtot, an unchanged K1 gives a
relative change in total receptor of (1/K1'after - 1/K1'before) / (1/K1'before).
From the Table 4 averages the paper reports -0.55 (computed with K1' rounded to
0.011 and 0.005); the unrounded averages carried by the models give -0.54.

```{r receptor-loss}
k1p_pre <- exp(ui_pre$theta[["lre50_hgp"]])
k1p_post <- exp(ui_post$theta[["lre50_hgp"]])
delta <- (1 / k1p_post - 1 / k1p_pre) / (1 / k1p_pre)
round(delta, 3)
stopifnot(abs(delta - (-0.55)) < 0.02)
```

**Free receptor during the challenge.** The Discussion reports that the free
receptor fraction falls during the challenge by about 15% before treatment and
8% after treatment; in Figure 5 these are drops in `r` of about 0.15 and 0.08
(fractions of the total receptor pool).

```{r free-receptor-drop}
drop_r <- sim |>
  group_by(treatment) |>
  summarise(r_start = first(r_free), r_end = last(r_free), drop = r_start - r_end)
knitr::kable(drop_r, digits = 3)
stopifnot(
  abs(drop_r$drop[drop_r$treatment == "Before treatment"] - 0.15) < 0.02,
  abs(drop_r$drop[drop_r$treatment == "After treatment (400 mg)"] - 0.08) < 0.02
)
```

**Peak glucose.** Table 4 reports the observed peak glucose `Gmax` (mean of
the individual data maxima: 2.71 g/L before, 2.00 g/L after). The
average-parameter model peaks lower (about 2.4 and 1.8 g/L), as it does in
Figure 5: the curve of averaged parameters is not the average of the
individual curves, and the observed maxima include measurement noise. The
relative reduction with treatment is similar.

```{r gmax}
gmax <- sim |>
  group_by(treatment) |>
  summarise(model_peak = max(Gc)) |>
  mutate(observed_gmax = ifelse(treatment == "Before treatment", 2.71, 2.00))
knitr::kable(gmax, digits = 2)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Two models for one structure.** The source fitted every subject twice and
  compared the two sets of individual estimates; it did not fit a treatment
  effect. The two files carry the Table 4 averages for each condition. No
  between-subject or residual variability is encoded: the Table 4 SDs describe
  the spread of individual smooth-profiling fits, and the method has no error
  model.
* **Glucagon distribution volume.** Table 2 prints VE = 9.6 L; Table 3, which
  the Methods cite as the source of the volumes, prints 19.6 L. The models use
  19.6 L: it gives the glucagon plateau of about 37 pmol/L shown in Figure 5 and
  the stated 2-3-fold rise over baseline, whereas 9.6 L would give about
  75 pmol/L.
* **Baseline insulin and glucagon digitised.** The average pre-challenge
  concentrations are not tabulated. `bl_glucagon` and `bl_insulin` were read
  from the 0-3 h segment of the Figure 5 curves (17.4 pmol/L and 10.5 mU/L
  before treatment; 24.0 pmol/L and 9.7 mU/L after). Override them in `ini()`
  to simulate an individual.
* **Baseline glucose derived.** Baseline glucose is computed from Eq 9 rather
  than supplied, so the model starts at its own steady state; it matches the
  Figure 5 baseline within digitisation error.
* **Challenge period only.** The model starts at the challenge (test hour 3)
  with endogenous insulin and glucagon secretion switched off. The pre-challenge
  steady state needs no simulation, and the paper's basal secretion rates
  (F-bar I, F-bar E) are neither fitted nor reported. Infusions must start at
  model time 0; dosing later lets insulin and glucagon decay from baseline
  first, which the source does not describe.
* **Units printed in Tables 1 and 4.** V1 and Vii are printed with units 1/h;
  dimensional analysis of Eq 8a requires g/L/h (see Units). Vid is printed as
  1/h and multiplies insulin in mU/L, so it is 1/h per mU/L. The values are
  used as printed.
* **Internalization rate in the Discussion.** The Discussion quotes kin
  averages of 21.022 and 12.05 1/h; Table 4 and supplementary Table 7 give
  21.5 and 12.1. The models use the tables.
* **kon unit.** Table 2 and the Methods give kon = 0.0036 1/pmol/h (written
  "(pM h)^-1" in the Methods); the identifiability code in the supplement uses
  6e-5 per minute, the same value.
* **Placebo comparison.** Supplementary Figure 6 overlays the before-treatment
  model on eight placebo subjects not used in fitting; those data are not
  available, so that figure is not reproduced.
